long_biography.plain_text:
Kracum studied at Carleton College and earned a chemistry master’s and MBA at the University of Chicago. After strategy consulting at Booz Allen Hamilton, he joined Wind Point in 1985. He later led a buyout of discount retailer Prange Way, serving as chairman and lead investor before returning to relaunch Wind Point’s institutional private-equity platform in 1996.

At Wind Point, Kracum helped establish a middle-market strategy built around operating executives, sector focus and active ownership. He recruited and mentored the next leadership generation, then gradually transferred responsibility before retiring from the firm’s front lines. He continues to serve as an independent fund manager and on corporate and nonprofit boards, bringing decades of private-markets experience to governance roles.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 99. Yachts International interviewed Rich Kracum aboard Alpha Waves and independently reproduced his Wind Point, education, geography and family context. SEC, Forbes, Carleton, Companies House and LinkedIn sources converge on the same Richard Robertson Kracum, leaving no plausible competing yacht-owner identity.

The authoritative relationship begins in 2020, while public vessel sources describe Alpha Waves as launched and delivered in 2023. The earlier date plausibly marks an order, construction project or initial ownership relationship, but no reviewed source explains the database convention. It is excluded from the biographies.

SuperYacht Network reports Alpha Waves at 40.54 metres and 385 GT, while SuperYacht Times reports 41.14 metres and 386 GT. The differences may reflect model length, measurement conventions or updated tonnage. The direct owner interview establishes the correct vessel independently, so the small specification discrepancies do not impair identity resolution.

Yachts International had a commercial connection to Kracum: the article states that Wind Point previously invested in its parent, Active Interest Media, and that Kracum retained a minority shareholding. It remains valuable as a direct on-board interview but is corroborated by SEC, Forbes, Carleton, Companies House and ACG sources for all core career claims.

Forbes.com has no dedicated Rich or Richard Kracum person profile. The Forbes article naming him as a Wind Point co-founder is an exact independent source but does not satisfy the verified-profile contract, so no Forbes social link is proposed.

The upstream 1955 birth year conflicts with current and repeated SEC filings giving December 13, 1954. Companies House independently gives December 1954, and the age in the late-2023 interview is consistent with 1954. The dossier therefore proposes day 13, month December and correction of the year to 1954.

Companies House gives the full name Richard Robertson Kracum, while most professional sources use Richard R. or Rich Kracum. The legal first and middle fields are proposed as Richard and Robertson, but the established display name Rich Kracum is preserved.

Wind Point's current website says the original firm was founded in 1984. Kracum joined in 1985 and later described re-founding or relaunching it with a partner in 1996; SEC, Forbes and Carleton call him a co-founder or founder. The Founder classification refers to the institutional Wind Point platform he helped build, not sole creation of the predecessor entity.

Self-made describes a career-based path through consulting, direct investment and partnership leadership. Wind Point's predecessor had S.C. Johnson family backing, but there is no evidence that Kracum inherited that capital or received a family transfer. The label does not imply he started without professional or institutional advantages.

Finance & Investments is the creation industry and current primary industry. Kracum is retired from day-to-day Wind Point work, but the latest SEC filing identifies continuing management of private-asset funds and multiple directorships. Public sources do not reveal whether finance assets constitute a majority of his personal balance sheet, so primary-industry confidence is lower than wealth-creation confidence.

Private equity is the only proposed tag. It satisfies the active taxonomy contract through decades of founder-level investing and current fund governance. Asset management was not added because it would describe the same platform more broadly and would not improve the minimum useful set.

The existing LinkedIn profile matches the Wind Point, Carleton and Chicago identity and is preserved. The rkracum Instagram handle is plausible and remains upstream, but no strong indexed source independently exposes enough profile content to verify or reject it; no change is proposed.

No reliable source establishes a birthplace, birth country, second nationality, suffix, honorific title, secondary residence or personal website. Minneapolis is documented only as where Kracum grew up, not where he was born.

The replacement biography removes transient age, empty markup and the unexplained '4o' artifact. Both biographies are source-invisible and sale-independent, omit Alpha Waves and personal wealth estimates, and distinguish his historical founder work from current governance.
